## 💱 69 currencies

**Settings → General → Currency**, or the welcome screen, now offers 41 more currencies, 69 in all (#12, #14):

- **Arab:** Mauritanian ouguiya, Djiboutian franc, Somali shilling and Comorian franc, next to the 17 already there.
- **Asia and the Pacific:** Hong Kong dollar, Indonesian rupiah, Singapore dollar, South Korean won, New Taiwan dollar, Thai baht, Philippine peso, Malaysian ringgit, Vietnamese dong, Bangladeshi taka and New Zealand dollar.
- **Europe:** Swedish krona, Norwegian and Danish krone, Polish złoty, Czech koruna, Hungarian forint, Romanian leu, Bulgarian lev, Icelandic króna, Russian ruble, Ukrainian hryvnia, Serbian dinar, Albanian lek, Bosnia-Herzegovina convertible mark, Macedonian denar, Moldovan leu and Belarusian ruble.
- **The Americas:** Mexican, Chilean, Colombian and Argentine peso, Brazilian real and Peruvian sol.
- **Africa:** South African rand, Nigerian naira and Kenyan shilling.

Each shows its usual decimals, and voice entry understands their names ("250 kronor", "40 pesos and 50 centavos"). As before, it's one currency for all your data: switching relabels amounts, it doesn't convert them.

## 🔍 Search the currency list

The currency list now has a search field: type a code (**SEK**) or a name, in English or Arabic, to find a currency without scrolling.

## Download
**Android**
- Also on **[F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/packages/ace.software.pocketsense/)**, which keeps it updated. It ships these same signed APKs, so you can switch between the two and keep your data.
- **`PocketSense-v2.4.1-arm64-v8a.apk`**: almost all modern Android phones. Use this one if unsure.
- `PocketSense-v2.4.1-armeabi-v7a.apk`: older 32-bit phones
- `PocketSense-v2.4.1-x86_64.apk`: emulators and Chromebooks

Installs as an update over any earlier version and keeps your data.

**Linux (x86_64)**: pick one.
- **Debian, Ubuntu, Mint:** `PocketSense-v2.4.1-linux-x64.deb`
  ```sh
  sudo apt install ./PocketSense-v2.4.1-linux-x64.deb
  ```
- **Fedora, openSUSE:** `PocketSense-v2.4.1-linux-x64.rpm`
  ```sh
  sudo dnf install ./PocketSense-v2.4.1-linux-x64.rpm   # or: sudo zypper install
  ```
- **Any distro:** `PocketSense-v2.4.1-linux-x64.AppImage`. Make it executable and run it.
- **Any distro:** `PocketSense-v2.4.1-linux-x64.tar.gz`. Unpack it and run `./PocketSense/pocket_sense`.

All need glibc 2.35 or newer and a running keyring (GNOME Keyring or KWallet). With the AppImage or the tarball you also need GTK 3, and `parecord` for voice entry (`pulseaudio-utils` on Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora, `libpulse` on Arch).
